purpose: Versioned acceptance specification and review contract against the agreed guided workbench. Function, design fidelity, aesthetics and discoverability are independent verdicts. This file records no execution pass and authorizes no UI change, build, publication or release.

accepted_user_decisions: Browser/WebAssembly is the first reference user experience; GTK and console adapt the same semantic contract.
Profiles own key-guide/status text, colours and row count.

Visible Program console and Tools & Profiles controls toggle show/hide across browser and GTK; cross-pane selection retains state. This newer decision overrides prototype selection-only demo handlers.
Native executable programs belong to desktop hosts only.
.profile.the -> Build profile/Apply profile; ordinary .the -> Build macro/Run macro; compiled profile -> .profile.rxbin.
GTK margins, gaps and control sizing require an explicit aesthetic acceptance review; small margins and large buttons are concerns to assess, not implementation-approved defaults.
Command response/error history is reviewable, explicitly clearable and filtered to the current file; this does not add a command-line recall requirement.

prototype.integrity: Use the frozen reference manifest/SHA supplied beside the reference. Do not mutate the reference to make an implementation pass.
prototype.status: Approved visual/interaction principles; illustrative handlers and mock details are not evidence of functional approval.

supporting_documents.use: Fixed scope authority; current implementation statements can age and require source/artifact verification.
Core/driver ownership, mutation and parser testing contracts.
Current profile/navigation/footer semantics; conflicts with approved reference require a decision, not silent precedence.
Current native routes/limits and claimed regression coverage; not design approval.
Existing regression evidence leads and separate qualification boundaries.

authority.precedence: Explicit newer user decisions, then agreed design/scope and resolved decisions. Existing implementation or prior PASS never redefines design. Record unresolved conflicts in decision register.

requirements.title: Recognisable editor at startup
requirements.principle: The guided workbench starts as a usable editor; ordinary text does not require tool setup.
observable_checkpoints: A fresh workspace identifies CRXTHE, current file, saved/dirty state and Text role without requiring a runner.
Editor, prefix/ruler, command entry, profile status and key guide remain recognisable; Files, Program console and Tools & Profiles have distinct destinations.
Selecting a file or declaring an object does not execute a tool.

requirements.title: File lifecycle and byte preservation
requirements.principle: Open, New, Save, Close and cancellation protect the actual document and its saved bytes.
observable_checkpoints: Open and New create or select real file-ring entries; Save success means the selected provider completed its write.
Dirty and pending edits are visible; closing or leaving cannot silently discard them; cancellation retains text, caret, selection and command draft.
Save and reopen reproduce exact fixture bytes; failures retain the modified buffer and a retry route.

requirements.title: Pane buttons toggle and retain state
requirements.principle: A visible pane control shows its target, hides that active visible target on repetition, and restores the target on the next activation. Another already-open sibling may become rendered after target hiding; this does not mean the target failed to hide.
observable_checkpoints: For Program console and Tools & Profiles, activate while target hidden -> target shown; activate that same visible target control -> target hidden; activate again -> target restored. Inspect target visibility independently of whether the auxiliary area still renders another open pane.
Selecting another pane activates that destination without discarding either pane state; repeated toggles work in wide and compact layouts.
Toggling or switching preserves the program job, unsent input, output, reader position/selection, source caret and editor bytes.
Files is a distinct browser workspace view. A native Open chooser does not establish a persistent GTK file list.

Record logically open, selected and actually rendered states separately for every pane. Post-hide sibling selection/latent-open policy is D08, not an invented requirement to close the whole auxiliary area.

requirements.title: THE editing and Unicode invariants

canonical_references.code_region: editor grid, prefix and status: lines 128-128

requirements.principle: The visible editor remains THE, including pending records, prefix commands, selection and undo.
observable_checkpoints: Unicode insertion, selection replacement and pending-record operations use logical positions and never split a grapheme unexpectedly.
Prefix and command focus are distinguishable from file editing; navigation and nonediting controls preserve insertion point.
For each mutation assert text, cursor, selection, dirty state, pending state and saved/reopened bytes; do not infer success from an action receipt alone.

requirements.title: Commands, menus and keyboard discovery
requirements.principle: Menus expose coherent tasks while profile key definitions and THE command entry remain authoritative.
observable_checkpoints: File/Edit/View/Tools/Help destinations are grouped consistently; custom profile menu extensions survive host grouping.
F10/default Menu, arrows, Enter, Escape and Shift-Tab give a complete keyboard route; ordinary Tab keeps its profile editing meaning.

Current-file command/response/error history can be shown, hidden and explicitly cleared without clearing another file’s history. Reviewing or clearing it preserves the unsent command draft, caret and focused target and never executes a command.
Menu shortcut labels reflect actual profile authority; a replaced key binding is not overridden by a host accelerator.

requirements.title: Purpose-specific file actions and build identity
requirements.principle: The current file role determines explicit Build, Run or Apply actions and their source revision.
observable_checkpoints: .profile.the offers Build profile then Apply profile; ordinary .the offers Build macro then Run macro; compiled profiles use .profile.rxbin.
.crexx offers Build source then Run with cREXX; .rexx and registered .bas runners can Run directly without profile setup.
Build captures the unsaved source identity/revision; edited or switched sources cannot run or apply an older artifact accidentally.
Build/profile output belongs to Build results in Tools & Profiles; it does not erase Program output, selection or input draft.

requirements.title: Explicit language and RXBIN execution
requirements.principle: Run uses an identified permitted adapter and never silently substitutes a different language or host.
observable_checkpoints: Classic Rexx, cREXX Level B/G and MiniBASIC examples have visible routes and expected program output in a matching enabled bundle.
MiniBASIC runs on first open through the stock association; its editable profile is an override, not a setup prerequisite.
An explicit compiled RXBIN path or imported image runs as a program, not as editor text or a profile.
Unsupported language, image cohort or host capability is visibly refused with a useful reason and recovery route.

requirements.title: Program input, completion and recovery
requirements.principle: Program I/O is separate from editor commands and profile/build output.
observable_checkpoints: Program console identifies stdout, stderr, source snapshot, state and completion; starting a job does not save or mutate its source.
Labelled Program input sends one record only by Enter/Send, accepts Unicode and an explicit empty record, and supports EOF.
Paste alone never submits; invalid multiline input is refused before changing the draft.
Stop and runtime errors leave the editor usable; a subsequent valid job can run without reloading the editor.

requirements.title: Profile source, compiled selection and startup
requirements.principle: Profiles are edited as source, built and explicitly applied; applied and persisted states are distinct.
observable_checkpoints: Tools & Profiles separates Profiles, File types & tools and Build results, identifies active selection and gives an Edit source route.
Build profile -> Apply profile publishes an immutable matching artifact; editing requires another build; success can be selected for restart.
Apply compiled profile admits .profile.rxbin explicitly without opening binary text; compiled-only selection explains source availability.
A failed build/activation retains the prior published composition and selection; a persistence failure says applied for this session only.

requirements.title: Profile-built actions, menus and explicit macros
requirements.principle: Profiles and macros assemble bounded workbench objects without frontend changes or automatic execution.
observable_checkpoints: An explicitly activated user profile can add, replace and remove an owned safe action/menu entry without duplication.
A user-authored macro source can be edited, built and explicitly invoked from its admitted menu route; declarations and file opening do not invoke it.
Explicit macro, prefix and synonym routes preserve their distinct meanings; unavailable browser admissions explain the refusal.
Profile/key/menu authority does not confer native filesystem, process or network authority; a restrictive current implementation is a gap where agreed behavior is mandatory.

requirements.title: Profile-owned status, key guide and colours

canonical_references.code_region: response, command, key guide and status: lines 42-47

requirements.principle: Profiles own status/key-guide text, colour and row count; host presentation follows the published rows.
observable_checkpoints: Custom named footer text, ordering, colour and multiple/zero guide rows render from profile data and survive file switching/inheritance.
Status, command and response areas remain distinct from file bytes. A quiet idle response is acceptable under resolved D01; meaningful responses remain visible and profile-owned.
Console colour roles update immediately from the active file profile without losing job, draft, reader selection or focus.
Clicking informational status/footer areas preserves the existing keyboard target and logical insertion point.

For the stock/reference profile, compare the agreed prototype geometry: response above THE command, followed by key guide then status. Current implementation documentation cannot approve a departure. Preserve custom profile text, colours, row count and explicitly configured positions; D04 is the implementation design task, not a waiver of stock reference fidelity.

requirements.title: Clipboard follows the focused target
requirements.principle: Cut, Copy, Paste, Select all and Undo operate on the focused editable or readable target.
observable_checkpoints: Source selection replacement is atomic; one supported Undo restores bytes, caret and dirty state; Copy includes pending source text.
Command, prefix, Program input, output reader and file-field targets keep their own clipboard and edit rules; output is read-only.
Clipboard denial, oversized/invalid paste or unsupported context gives a visible reason before deleting source, changing draft or losing selection.
Native entry Undo limitations are explicit and never undo the unrelated source file.

requirements.title: Responsive layout preserves access and state
requirements.principle: Wide, narrow, short and touch layouts keep core tasks reachable and retain the same session state.
observable_checkpoints: A wide layout can show editor beside an auxiliary pane; narrow layouts adapt placement rather than clipping essential input or controls.
Menu, current-file actions, command entry, pane controls and modal dismissal remain reachable at the specified sample sizes.
Resizing, opening/hiding panes and font/zoom changes preserve source caret, pending edit, job, draft, reader position and selection.
Touch targets and scrolling permit the specified phone journeys; short-height navigation is reviewed as a distinct adaptation.

requirements.title: Reader stability and named panes

canonical_references.code_region: separate Program and build destinations: lines 143-146

requirements.principle: Program readers and profile-published LOG, DOCUMENT, form and optional file-field panes have explicit state and safe operations.
observable_checkpoints: New output follows only at latest; scrolling back/selecting retains position and selection, shows unread output and offers return-to-latest.
Build/profile updates do not switch Program pages or steal focus; hiding readers does not stop their producer.
Named LOG routes retain output; DOCUMENT is read-only and follows the live source; independent forms stage and Submit/Cancel without file mutation.
Optional CTLCHAR file fields protect fixed spans; Apply is one core edit group, Save is explicit, stale Apply refuses without losing drafts.

requirements.title: Settings separate presentation from editor scope

canonical_references.code_region: Settings sections and driver appearance: lines 148-154

requirements.principle: Appearance belongs to the driver; Editor settings apply existing commands to the current file and expose profile defaults separately.
observable_checkpoints: GTK Appearance offers installed monospace font/point size, reset, consistent metrics and persistence with visible session-only failure.
Browser Appearance explains browser zoom; console font is controlled by the terminal emulator, not a Rexx font setting.
Editor settings show live line-number/prefix/tab values, apply only to the current file, and do not silently rewrite profile source.
Edit profile defaults and Tools & Profiles lead to their existing destinations; Settings navigation preserves unsaved source and caret.

requirements.title: Native conventions and host boundaries
requirements.principle: The same operations use appropriate native routes while capability and qualification boundaries remain explicit.
observable_checkpoints: GTK macOS has native application About/Settings/Quit placement plus a keyboard fallback; other GTK desktops use in-window menu routes.
About gives actual version, licence/credits and available capabilities without implying an installed or release-qualified package.
Native executable programs, including optionally configured ooRexx, belong to desktop adapters only; browser refusal does not silently select a remote or other runner.
Console uses terminal navigation/presentation and real PTY evidence; one desktop/browser result does not qualify other OS, browser, packaging or installation cohorts.

requirements.title: Scope dispositions and coherent design tasks
requirements.principle: Separate genuine scope/sequencing dispositions from reference interpretation and implementation design work; unresolved records never waive observed mandatory failures.
observable_checkpoints: D01 is resolved: quiet idle is acceptable, meaningful responses remain profile-owned; no permanent Ready text is required.
Record one consolidated scope/sequencing disposition for D02 Redo, D03 Save as/source transfer and D06 proposed GTK persistent Files view.

Develop D04 stock geometry/custom profile rendering, D05 compact navigation, D07 spacing/control proportions and D08 sibling state as one coherent design proposal rather than separate user permission questions.
Default geometry follows the agreed prototype; current stock documentation does not approve departure. Preserve all custom profile authority.
Observed mandatory toggle, state-preservation, editing, reference-fidelity or aesthetic gaps keep their failure finding; DecisionNeeded covers only an unresolved checkpoint.

requirements.title: Aesthetic comfort, spacing and control scale

canonical_references.code_region: shell rhythm, control padding and layout: lines 11-31
pane sections, fields, settings and dialogs: lines 48-77

requirements.principle: The interface must be visually comfortable and coherent: readable content, deliberate margins and rhythm, proportional controls and a clear task hierarchy appropriate to its native platform.
observable_checkpoints: Review GTK toolbar, pane bodies, file actions, Tools & Profiles sections, Settings and About for content crowded against containers and for buttons disproportionate to labels/font.

Measure actual container insets, related/unrelated control gaps, row rhythm, label/font/control bounding boxes and usable editor/reader area; pair measurements with screenshots and a human aesthetic judgement.
Compare reference hierarchy and density with the actual platform at the same logical size and comparable text scale; native theme differences alone are not failures.
Distinguish comfortable pointer controls from coarse-pointer touch targets; the prototype 44 px coarse-pointer rule does not require desktop GTK buttons to be touch-sized.
No clipped labels, unreadable text, cramped focus rings, accidental collisions or inaccessible controls; repeated sections use a coherent spacing/control rhythm.
Separate user preference/comfort findings from objective clipping/measurement and proposed numeric thresholds; obtain D07 before making invented pixel values a golden.

decisions.subject: Idle response reference annotation
decisions.question: Resolved annotation: the mock Ready text is illustrative, not a permanent idle-message requirement.
decisions.authority_conflict: Resolved by doc/ui-acceptance/reference/README.md#authority-and-interpretation and the first-launch contract: the mock literal Ready does not require permanent idle content.
decisions.recommended_resolution: Accept a quiet idle response. Show meaningful command/error responses when they occur, with profile-owned response/status presentation. Preserve this trace ID without treating it as an open permission question.
decisions.resolution: Quiet idle is acceptable. The prototype literal Ready is sample content; meaningful responses and profile authority remain mandatory.

decisions.question: Does the prototype Redo item commit this milestone to a real Redo operation, and what are its source/native-field semantics?
decisions.authority_conflict: Prototype line 112 shows Redo; its handler only writes a mock response. No Redo acceptance is inferred from that handler.

decisions.subject: Save as and source import/export
decisions.question: Confirm milestone treatment of Save as and the baseline single-file UTF-8 import/export journey, including collisions and the 2 MiB limit.
decisions.authority_conflict: Prototype File menu contains Save as; fixed scope baseline requires bounded source import/export; implementation guides describe their absence. Absence does not waive the baseline.
decisions.recommended_resolution: Retain bounded source import/export as a baseline requirement and include Save as in a coherent file-workflow proposal. Ask for one explicit scope/sequencing disposition where needed; implementation absence remains a gap until that disposition, rather than an automatic deferral.

decisions.subject: Default footer geometry and custom-profile rendering
decisions.question: Design task: align stock footer geometry with the agreed prototype while preserving custom profile authority.
decisions.authority_conflict: Prototype line 128 is the expected stock geometry. Current first-launch text describes an implementation and does not approve geometric departure. Custom profile text, colours, row count and explicit settings remain authoritative.
decisions.recommended_resolution: Use the agreed prototype stock geometry: response above THE command, followed by key guide then status. Prepare one coherent implementation design that renders custom profile text, colours, row count and configured positions correctly. Current stock documentation does not approve a departure; no separate user question is needed for each row or key-label position.

decisions.subject: Compact navigation and short-height Expand
decisions.question: Design task: propose one coherent compact/short-window navigation adaptation, including any needed Expand/Return route.
decisions.authority_conflict: Prototype supplies narrow stacking, but no short-height Expand contract. All existing pane controls must still toggle per the newer explicit user decision.
decisions.recommended_resolution: Present narrow/short screenshots and one consistent navigation proposal alongside D04/D07/D08. Keep pane toggles, visible access, dismissal and state preservation mandatory; use an explicit Expand/Return route only where the compact design needs it. Do not seek separate approval for every breakpoint or control.

decisions.subject: Persistent GTK Files list
decisions.question: Should a persistent Files view be a shared browser/GTK capability?
decisions.authority_conflict: The graphical reference depicts a Files affordance, GTK currently has a native chooser, and the user proposes making a file list common. Record the missing design capability and decide its implementation sequencing; a native chooser is not a persistent file list.
decisions.recommended_resolution: Present the persistent GTK Files view as a distinct proposed capability with a scope/sequencing recommendation. Native Open remains an opening route, not file-list parity. Do not silently make the proposal mandatory or treat its absence as an approved shared-feature exception.

decisions.subject: Quantitative aesthetic tolerances
decisions.question: Design task: derive comfortable native spacing and control proportions from measured evidence, then propose any useful platform tolerances.
decisions.authority_conflict: The user requires aesthetic review and raised small GTK margins/large buttons. No exact pixel target or 8 px golden was approved. Observable legibility, coherent hierarchy and usable comfortable spacing remain assessable now.
decisions.recommended_resolution: Include measured GTK insets, gaps, button/font proportions and revised screenshots in the same coherent design proposal as D04/D05/D08. Use the agreed hierarchy and native platform context; do not request a pixel-by-pixel user decision or invent an 8 px golden. Aesthetic defects remain assessable before numeric tolerances are selected.

decisions.subject: Pane state after hiding the target
decisions.question: Design task: specify coherent selected/rendered/logically-open pane state after the clicked target is hidden.
decisions.authority_conflict: The clicked pane must toggle hidden/shown. The user has not required the entire auxiliary area to disappear when an already-open sibling can render. Record target visibility, logical openness and selected/rendered pane independently.
decisions.recommended_resolution: Propose a predictable sibling-selection and latent-open policy together with compact navigation, while preserving all pane data. The clicked visible target must already hide/show correctly; another open sibling may render afterward. Do not ask the user to approve each state transition or require the entire auxiliary area to disappear.

values.Pass: All applicable assertions on this axis were observed with matching evidence; no unresolved decision is passed by inference.
values.Fail: At least one applicable assertion was observed to fail; describe actual versus expected.
values.Partial: Only a defined subset was exercised or evidence is incomplete; list the untested remainder. Never means a weaker Pass.
values.NotRun: This axis was not exercised or observed. Existing tests, a screenshot or an implementer replay do not imply first-user discoverability.
values.NotApplicable: An explicitly permitted platform/optional variant does not apply; record the narrow reason and authority. Missing mandatory UI, unavailable required adapters and skipped displays are not N/A.
values.DecisionNeeded: An explicit unresolved design/scope checkpoint prevents judgement. Identify decision ID and still report independently testable assertions.

rules: Keep all four verdicts separate per platform/sample/variant; never average into one PASS.
Blocked execution names the blocker; unobserved axes stay NotRun or Partial. It does not mean NotApplicable.
A mandatory unavailable/refused route is a functional/design gap unless refusal itself is the expected host boundary.
DecisionNeeded applies only to affected checkpoints; it does not waive already mandatory assertions.
Prior tests and reference screenshots are evidence leads, never approval or golden outputs.

sampling.goal_first_protocol: A fresh or reset independent participant receives only goal_first_prompt and allowed task materials. sampling.decision_gating: Resolve only a genuinely unsettled checkpoint before judging that detail. required_observations: Container insets: text/fields/buttons are not crowded against pane, toolbar or dialog boundaries; record actual top/right/bottom/left insets where a concern occurs.
Gaps and rhythm: related controls read as a group; unrelated groups have separation; repeated rows/sections follow a coherent rhythm.
Control scale: compare button height/width and padding to its label/font and neighbouring fields; flag disproportionate pointer controls and crowded controls with screenshots.
Readability and hierarchy: title, current file, role/action row, source, pane heading, help, status and input remain distinguishable at actual zoom/font.
Density and comfort: enough source/output is usable for the task; pane controls do not overwhelm content; do not sacrifice comfortable targets for arbitrary density.
Native platform fit: compare GTK with its active theme/font and native menus, browser with zoom/touch mode, console with emulator/cell geometry.
Input mode: use comfortable pointer controls for desktop; evaluate the prototype 44 px minimum only for coarse-pointer browser samples, with actual device/emulation recorded.
aesthetics_rubric.judgement: Record objective measurements and observed human comfort separately. Pass requires a coherent, readable, comfortable presentation at the exercised checkpoints. Fail identifies a concrete visual defect or supported comfort finding. Partial lists unreviewed surfaces. No independent aesthetic observation means NotRun; do not infer beauty from function or test success.
aesthetics_rubric.threshold_policy: No unapproved fixed pixel golden. Measured spacing/control targets are design work under D07 and should be proposed coherently with D04/D05/D08, not as pixel-by-pixel permission questions. Their absence never waives clipping, poor hierarchy, disproportionate controls, crowded margins or the required aesthetic review.

decision_summary.handling: These are advisory dispositions, not eight user-permission questions. Scope-owner records need one consolidated scope/sequencing disposition; implementation-design records belong in one coherent design proposal. Resolved reference annotations require no new approval.
decision_summary.mandatory_gap_rule: Observed failures of already mandatory assertions remain Fail/Partial findings. DecisionNeeded applies only to the genuinely unresolved checkpoint and never masks pane-toggle, state-preservation, reference stock geometry, profile authority or aesthetic defects.
